components.name: Gradient
components.description:
ℹ️ This component addresses gradients not being natively supported with Figma variables.
ℹ️ To use this component, insert it where a gradient is required and resize as necessary. By default, the gradient is using the background hex code (not variable) from each theme and is a left to right linear gradient with 100% to 0% opacity, respectively. If you need to flip the orientation of the gradient, simply use the keyboard shortcut Shift + H to flip as desired.

components.name: Mosaic grid
components.description:
Mosaic Grid | Snow Cone Design SystemTo use this component begin by placing it in a desired Auto layout and set its "Horizontal resizing" property to "Fill container."
Paste your image fills as you normally do and observe that the aspect ratio is maintained
NOTE: After pasting your image fill into the top left or bottom right aspect ratios you will notice that they resize slightly. To resolve this simply set their "Vertical resizing" properties back to "Fill container"
Choose between the available gutter options, or add your own. To fine tune specific gutter values you will need to do a little basic math.
First choose a desired gutter size. In this example, we're going to use 32px.
Select the center Aspect ratio square by Cmd + Clicking on it, then pressing Shift + Enter on your keyboard to select its parent frame titled "Square"
Divide 32px by 3 (10.67) and then multiply that value by 2 (21.34). Enter this value for the padding on all 4 sides. For best results, enter several decimal places. ie. 21.3444444444 vs 21.34
For the other 4 aspect ratios, divide 32px by 3 and use this as the value for the padding on their parent frames. Do not multiply the value by 2 as we did in step 7. In this example, the value we would use would be 10.6666666666 vs 10.67. For the top left aspect ratio, apply this value to the bottom padding, for the top right aspect ratio apply this padding to the left padding, for the bottom left aspect ratio apply this value to the top padding, and for the bottom right aspect ratio apply this value to the top padding
To take this even further, you can now set all of this up via variables to reduce the number of variants needed
Do not resize this component from the top or bottom edge or the corners
Do not hold down Shift on your keyboard while resizing
It is ok to hold down Option on your keyboard while resizing
If the component is not maintaining its aspect ratio, check that the "Vertical resizing" property is set to "Hug contents" instead of "Fixed"

CreditPlease also consider checking out Vitalii's original Aspect Ratio component file, as he is the original creator of the Aspect Ratio component that I'm using.
Shameless plugAdditionally, here is my community file specific to the Aspect Ratio - Vertical Resize component used in this file. I have included it in this file however, but if you're interested in checking out the background behind how this component was created, please feel free to check it out!
YouTube ChannelPlease consider checking out my YouTube channel for Figma tips and tricks.

components.name: AI layer - Background
components.description:
In contrast to baseline Carbon, the AI layer is intended to identify instances of AI at-a-glance. This enables better recognition and recall in a way that is identifiable across any IBM product, while sharing the same base principles as the existing Carbon design language.


ℹ️ By default, the background layer and border are visible. You may need to remove one or both depending on the component needs.


Reference: AI Layer Guidance Anatomy | Scalability

components.name: AI layer - Field
components.description:
In contrast to baseline Carbon, the AI layer is intended to identify instances of AI at-a-glance. This enables better recognition and recall in a way that is identifiable across any IBM product, while sharing the same base principles as the existing Carbon design language.


ℹ️ By default, the background layer and border are visible. You may need to remove one or both depending on the component needs.


Reference: AI Layer Guidance Anatomy | Scalability

components.name: AI label
components.description:
The AI label (formerly AI slug) is intended for any scenarios where something is being generated by (or with) AI with the goal of reinforcing AI transparency, accountability, and explainability at any level of the interface.


Reference: AI label usage guidance

components.name: AI explainability popover
components.description:
AI explainability popover appears when the user interacts with the AI label. The explainability popover contains more detailed information about how the information was generated.


ℹ️ The explainability popover heading has two options that use two different type tokens: Confidence score and Detail. Use the Confidence score option to highlight the percentage confidence the AI has in the explainability popover information. Use the Detail option to provide more background in the heading. Use the Callout heading modifier in Figma to switch as needed.


Reference: AI Explainability Popover
